description: We are a team of innovators, engineers, and problem-solvers building smart tech solutions for future Mars exploration. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we are tackling the growing issue of Martian orbital and surface debris to keep future missions safe, sustainable, and ready for human arrival.
summary:
Martian Core is an interactive, educational web application designed to help students, kids, and the public explore human-made space artifacts and debris on the Moon and Mars. Built around two iconic off-world hardware milestones, the Apollo 11 "Eagle" Lunar Module in the Sea of Tranquility and NASA’s Ingenuity Mars Helicopter in Jezero Crater, our platform turns real NASA mission data into an engaging, hands-on learning experience.
Through a first-person astronaut visor simulation, interactive size and gravity comparisons, a clue-based quiz, and a live community debate on whether space artifacts should be preserved, recycled, or returned to Earth, Martian Core directly addresses the challenge of off-world space debris awareness and sustainability.
As humanity prepares for permanent lunar bases and crewed Mars missions, protecting historic landing sites and managing inactive hardware is critical. Our project inspires the next generation of explorers to think responsibly about how we explore and preserve other worlds.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
Martian Core is an interactive, browser-based educational platform that transforms real NASA mission data about human-made hardware on the Moon and Mars into a hands-on space adventure. Focusing on two iconic off-world artifacts, the Apollo 11 Lunar Module ("Eagle") on the Moon and NASA’s Ingenuity Mars Helicopter on Mars, users can switch between planetary environments, explore telemetry and mission profiles, compare off-world mass and gravity against everyday objects, test their knowledge in an interactive clue quiz, and vote in a live community debate on whether retired spacecraft should be preserved as heritage monuments, recycled for future bases, or returned to Earth.


Benefits & Intended Impact
Most space debris education focuses solely on Low Earth Orbit, leaving younger learners unaware of the growing number of inactive landers, rovers, and aircraft resting on the Moon and Mars. Martian Core bridges this gap by making planetary sustainability accessible, fun, and memorable for kids and students. Our intended impact is to inspire the next generation of engineers and explorers to balance scientific discovery with responsible environmental stewardship on other worlds.


Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend Development: HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript for fast, zero-dependency browser performance across desktop and mobile devices.
  • AI & Prototyping: Claude AI for rapid interactive code generation and UI structuring.
  • Deployment & Hosting: Netlify Drop for instant cloud hosting and public access.
  • Data Sources: Official NASA NSSDCA Master Catalog records, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) coordinates, and NASA/JPL Mars 2020 mission telemetry.
Creativity & Design Considerations
Rather than presenting static tables of space statistics, we designed Martian Core around active participation, combining a first-person astronaut visor experience, relatable real-world scale comparisons (such as comparing the 2,034 kg Apollo descent stage and 1.8 kg Ingenuity helicopter to everyday items), and an ethical "What Happens If It Returns?" ranking board. Our team carefully considered accessibility, age-appropriate language, fast load times, and scientific accuracy so both young learners and aerospace judges can enjoy the experience seamlessly.
